5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 4

Comparatives

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Compare two people, animals or things (comparar dos cosas)
  • Form comparatives with -er and more
  • Learn the irregular comparatives better and worse
  • Use than, as… as and not as… as
  • Make comparisons stronger with much, a lot and a bit
  • Take a first look at superlatives
  • Compare places and animals with real data and write a comparison

Para pensar

Una jirafa mide unos 5 metros y un elefante, unos 3. ¿Cómo dirías en inglés que la jirafa es más alta?

Explicación

1. What is a comparative?

A comparative is the form of an adjective we use to compare two people, animals or things. «My brother is older than me.» «A plane is faster than a train.» «Maths is more difficult than Art for me.»

The word than introduces the second thing: «A than B». En castellano: «más alto que», «más rápido que». En inglés, con los adjetivos cortos no decimos «more tall», sino que el adjetivo cambia: taller. Así que hay que fijarse en el número de sílabas.

2. Short adjectives: -er

With short adjectives (one syllable) we add -er: tall → taller, small → smaller, fast → faster, old → older, long → longer, cold → colder, short → shorter, strong → stronger.

«Antarctica is colder than Spain.» «The Nile is longer than the Ebro.» «My grandfather is older than my grandmother.» The adjective doesn't change for plural: «These boxes are smaller than those boxes».

3. Spelling changes

Some short adjectives change a little. 1. Ending in -e: add only -r: nice → nicer, large → larger, safe → safer. 2. Consonant + vowel + consonant: double the last letter: big → bigger, hot → hotter, thin → thinner, fat → fatter, sad → sadder.

3. Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y: change y to -ier: happy → happier, funny → funnier, easy → easier, heavy → heavier, busy → busier. «Today is hotter than yesterday.» «This joke is funnier than yours!»

4. Long adjectives: more

With long adjectives (two syllables or more, not ending in -y) we put more in front: beautiful → more beautiful, expensive → more expensive, interesting → more interesting, dangerous → more dangerous, important → more important, famous → more famous.

«A shark is more dangerous than a dolphin.» «This book is more interesting than the film.» Ojo: nunca juntes las dos formas: «more taller» o «more easier» están mal. O -er, o more.

5. Irregular: better, worse, further

A few adjectives are irregular. You must learn them: good → better (mejor), bad → worse (peor) and far → further or farther (más lejos).

«My handwriting is better than last year.» «The weather today is worse than yesterday.» «Madrid is further from the sea than Valencia.» Truco: nunca digas «gooder» ni «more good». Piensa en el castellano: tampoco decimos «más bueno que» cuando queremos decir «mejor».

6. A first look at superlatives

Comparatives compare two things. When we compare one thing with all the others in a group, we use the superlative. In Spanish: «el más alto», «la más bonita».

  • Short adjectives: the + adjective + -est: tall → the tallest, fast → the fastest, big → the biggest, happy → the happiest.
  • Long adjectives: the most + adjective: beautiful → the most beautiful, interesting → the most interesting.
  • Irregular: good → the best, bad → the worst, far → the furthest.

The spelling rules are the same as for comparatives: nice → the nicest, hot → the hottest, funny → the funniest.

We often add in + a place or group, or of + a number or period:

  • «The blue whale is the biggest animal in the world.»
  • «Lola is the tallest girl in my class.»
  • «It was the best day of my life!»

Compare the three forms: tall – taller – the tallest; good – better – the best. You will study superlatives in more detail in 6th grade.

Superlatives are perfect for records and quizzes: «What is the longest river in the world?» (the Nile or the Amazon: scientists still discuss it!) «What is the fastest land animal?» (the cheetah). «Which is the coldest continent?» (Antarctica). Make your own quiz and test your family.

7. As… as and not as… as

When two things are the same, we use as + adjective + as: «Lucía is as tall as Marta» (Lucía y Marta miden lo mismo). «This bag is as heavy as that one.»

For the opposite we use not as… as: «My bike isn't as fast as yours» (mi bici es menos rápida). This is a polite way to compare. The adjective doesn't change here: we never say «as taller as».

8. Much bigger, a bit taller

Sometimes the difference between two things is big and sometimes it is small. We can show this with words before the comparative:

  • Big difference: much, a lot, far. «An elephant is much bigger than a mouse.» «A plane is a lot faster than a bike.» «Summer in Seville is far hotter than in Santander.»
  • Small difference: a bit, a little, slightly. «I'm a bit taller than my sister.» «This book is a little more expensive than that one.»

Never use very with comparatives: say «much bigger», not «very bigger».

We can also repeat the comparative to show that something is changing: «It's getting colder and colder.» (cada vez más frío) «The film was more and more exciting.»

And to talk about two things that change together, we use the… the…: «The more you read, the better you write.» (Cuanto más lees, mejor escribes.) This is a very common expression in English!

9. Comparing with numbers

We can use comparatives with real data. Look at this information about animals: a cheetah runs at 110 km/h and a horse at 70 km/h. → «A cheetah is faster than a horse.» A blue whale weighs 150,000 kg and an elephant 6,000 kg. → «A blue whale is heavier than an elephant.»

We can also say how much: «A cheetah is much faster than a horse» (mucho más) or «Leo is a bit taller than Eva» (un poco más). These little words make your comparisons more precise.

10. Comparing places in Spain

Comparatives are very useful in Geography. Look at these real data about Spain and compare:

  • Mountains: the Teide, in Tenerife, is 3,715 metres high. The Mulhacén, in Granada, is 3,479 metres high. → «The Teide is higher than the Mulhacén.» In fact, the Teide is the highest mountain in Spain.
  • Rivers: the Tajo is about 1,000 kilometres long. The Ebro is about 930 kilometres long. → «The Tajo is longer than the Ebro.»
  • Cities: Madrid has more than 3 million people. Barcelona has about 1.6 million. → «Madrid is bigger than Barcelona.» But Barcelona is on the coast, so we can say: «Barcelona is closer to the sea.»
  • Weather: in August, Córdoba is often hotter than Bilbao. Bilbao is usually rainier than Córdoba.

When you write numbers in English, remember that we use a comma for thousands (3,715) and a point for decimals (1.6). It's the opposite of Spanish!

Now find data about your town or region and write three comparisons. You can use a map, an encyclopedia or a reliable website.

11. Reading: city or village?

Read Irene's text: «I live in Madrid, but my grandparents live in a small village in Soria. Madrid is bigger and noisier than the village. There are more shops and the buses are faster. But the village is quieter and the air is cleaner. The winters there are colder than in Madrid, and the stars at night are brighter. The village isn't as exciting as the city, but for me it's more relaxing. In summer, I think the village is better!»

Find six comparatives with -er and two with more. Which one is irregular?

12. Let's practise: compare and guess

Play «Who is it?» in pairs. Think of two classmates, two animals or two famous places, and give clues: «It is bigger than a cat, but smaller than a horse. It is more friendly than a wolf.» (Answer: a dog!)

Then write five sentences comparing your town with another town, or yourself last year and now: «Now I am taller. My English is better. My homework is more difficult.» Repaso: corto → -er; largo → more; irregulares better, worse; y siempre than.

13. Than me or than I am?

After than we often compare with a person. There are two correct ways to do it:

  • than + object pronoun (me, you, him, her, us, them). This is the most common in everyday English: «My brother is taller than me.» «She runs faster than him.» «They are older than us.»
  • than + subject pronoun + verb (I am, he is, they do…). This is a bit more formal: «My brother is taller than I am.» «She runs faster than he does.»

Don't say «taller than I» alone in normal conversation: it sounds strange. Choose than me or than I am.

We can also compare with a name or a noun: «Pablo is funnier than Marcos.» «Cats are quieter than dogs.»

And to avoid repeating a noun, use one or ones: «This T-shirt is nicer than that one.» «These shoes are cheaper than the red ones.»

Remember that in English we always need than, not «that» or «of»: «bigger than», never «bigger that».

14. Writing: cats or dogs?

A comparison text describes two things and shows how they are similar and different. Let's write one about cats and dogs. Follow these steps:

  1. Make a table with information about the two animals: size, food, character, care.
  2. Introduction: present the topic. «Cats and dogs are the most popular pets in Spain. But which is better for you?»
  3. Differences: use comparatives. «Dogs are usually bigger than cats. They are more active and they need more exercise: you must walk them every day. Cats are more independent and quieter.»
  4. Similarities: use both and as… as. «Both animals are friendly and intelligent. A cat can be as loving as a dog.»
  5. Conclusion: give your opinion. «I think dogs are better for active families, but cats are better for small flats. My favourite? Cats, of course!»

Use connectors to link your ideas: but, however, also, both, on the other hand.

Before you hand in your text, check: did you use than after every comparative? Did you spell the adjectives correctly (bigger, quieter, more active)?

Comparatives

Ejercicios

  1. Write the comparative: small, hot, funny, nice.

  2. Write the comparative: famous, dangerous, good, bad.

  3. Complete: «A car is ___ (fast) than a bike.»

  4. Complete: «Science is ___ (interesting) than TV.»

  5. Complete: «Today the weather is ___ (bad) than yesterday.»

  6. Correct: «My house is more big that yours.»

  7. Same height: Pol 1.40 m, Gal 1.40 m. Write a sentence.

  8. Write with not as… as: «Tennis is more popular than golf.»

  9. Translate: «El Teide es más alto que el Mulhacén.»

  10. Compare yourself now and when you were five (three sentences).

  11. Write the superlative: tall, big, happy, good.

  12. Complete: «An elephant is ___ bigger than a mouse.» (much / very)

  13. Complete: «My sister is taller than ___.» (I / me)

  14. Which is longer: the Tajo or the Ebro?

  15. Translate: «Cada vez más frío».

  16. Write a sentence with «the best … in».

  17. Correct: «This film is very more interesting that the book.»

  18. Complete: «The ___ you practise, the ___ you play.» (much, good)

  19. Use «one»: «This bag is heavier than that bag.»

  20. Write two similarities between cats and dogs using both and as… as.

  21. Find data about two Spanish cities and write four comparisons.

  22. Write a comparison text about two sports (introduction, differences, similarities, conclusion).

  23. Write the animal contest from the ant's point of view with five comparatives.

  24. Make a quiz of five questions for your class: «Which is bigger: … or …?»

Practica

  1. The comparative of «tall» is…

    1. A) more tall
    2. B) tallest
    3. C) taller

  2. The comparative of «big» is…

    1. A) bigger
    2. B) biger
    3. C) more big

  3. The comparative of «happy» is…

    1. A) happyer
    2. B) happier
    3. C) more happy

  4. The comparative of «beautiful» is…

    1. A) beautifuller
    2. B) more beautiful
    3. C) most beautiful

  5. The comparative of «good» is…

    1. A) gooder
    2. B) more good
    3. C) better

  6. «A plane is faster ___ a car.»

    1. A) than
    2. B) that
    3. C) as

  7. «This test is ___ than the last one.» (bad)

    1. A) badder
    2. B) more bad
    3. C) worse

  8. «Ana is ___ Laia.» (misma edad)

    1. A) older as
    2. B) as old as
    3. C) as older as

  9. The comparative of «nice» is…

    1. A) nicer
    2. B) niceer
    3. C) more nice

  10. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) My bag is heavier than yours.
    2. B) My bag is more heavier than yours.
    3. C) My bag is heavyer than yours.

  11. «The blue whale is ___ animal in the world.»

    1. A) the bigger
    2. B) the biggest
    3. C) bigger

  12. «A plane is ___ faster than a bike.»

    1. A) very
    2. B) more
    3. C) much

  13. «He is older than ___.»

    1. A) I
    2. B) me
    3. C) my

  14. «The ___ you read, the better you write.»

    1. A) more
    2. B) most
    3. C) much

  15. The Teide is ___ the Mulhacén.

    1. A) lower than
    2. B) as high as
    3. C) higher than

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el comparativo; Cuándo se añade -er y cuándo se usa more; Qué comparativos son irregulares; Cómo se dice que dos cosas son iguales con as… as.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

ComparativeCompara dos cosas: taller than.
than«que» en las comparaciones.
-erAdjetivos cortos: fast → faster.
-ierAcabados en -y: easy → easier.
moreAdjetivos largos: more expensive.
better / worseMejor / peor.
as… asIgual de: as tall as.
not as… asMenos: not as fast as.

than meHe is taller than me.

Soluciones

  1. C) Corto: + -er.
  2. A) CVC: doble g.
  3. B) -y → -ier.
  4. B) Largo: more.
  5. C) Irregular.
  6. A) Than = que.
  7. C) Irregular.
  8. B) as + adjetivo + as.
  9. A) Acaba en -e: + r.
  10. A) heavy → heavier, sin more.
  11. B) Superlative.
  12. C) Big difference.
  13. B) Object pronoun.
  14. A) The more… the better.
  15. C) 3,715 m vs 3,479 m.
